readonly.py:368-384. Doubled quote (377-380) is treated as an escape for all three quote types. For ' and " a backslash skips the next char (372-376). For backtick no backslash handling, matching MySQL identifiers. A backslash followed by the same quote raises UnsafeSqlError (373-374), so the one case where default mode and NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES/ANSI_QUOTES disagree about where the token ends is refused rather than guessed. Every other backslash pair is consumed identically under both modes, since the next char is not the quote. The claim's wording slightly understates this refusal, but token termination is consistent with MySQL in every accepted input. I did not run sqlglot to check its tokenizer, so that part is reasoned from the code, not executed. The recorded rejections concern other subjects.

readonly.py:395-398: after '--', a following char is accepted if ord<=32 or ==127, and an empty following (end of string) raises nothing. This matches MySQL's lexer rule (sql_lex.cc: '--' followed by my_isspace or my_iscntrl, i.e. whitespace 9-13/32 or control 0-31/127; NUL at end of input counts as control, so a trailing '--' is a comment). Any other following char is rejected as ambiguous, which is the fail-closed outcome, since MySQL treats it as two minus operators and sqlglot may treat it differently. I checked this from my knowledge of the MySQL lexer and manual, not from fetched sources.
